subject: Purchase order mapping concerns and commit-tier options
messages:
From: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor supplier form & pricing format

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement reviewed Redwood's pricing and we have a few process constraints before Finance will approve a PO.

- Our standard vendor form (attached) requires unit pricing and a unit of measure per line item. Variable per-token rates are hard for our AP system to reconcile.
- We cannot accept a single "usage-based" line without a defined unit price (e.g., $ / million tokens) and a firm description.
- We prefer fixed line items on the PO rather than a monthly reconciliation that references token counts, unless you can accept a Blanket PO + monthly invoicing cadence with line-item amounts.

Can you confirm how Redwood maps per-token pricing into a PO line-item? If you can provide a proposed PO mapping (one-pager) and confirm whether Redwood will sign our vendor form, that will speed approvals.

Attaching: Vendor_Supplier_Form.xlsx (our standard).

Best,
John Lee
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Systems

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor supplier form & pricing format

John — thanks for the note and for sharing the form. I appreciate the constraints from a bookkeeping standpoint. Quick reply with two practical options we see frequently:

1) Fixed monthly commitment (recommended for accounting)
   - Redwood issues a PO line: "Redwood Hosted API - Monthly Commitment" with a fixed USD amount (e.g., $25,000 / month).
   - We map that to an expected token allowance in a simple table (e.g., 500M tokens / month).
   - Overages billed as a separate line: "Token Overages (per 1M tokens) — $X" on monthly invoices.

2) Unitized per-token line items (if you prefer explicit unit pricing)
   - PO contains line item(s) like "Text-generation tokens — $Y per 1,000,000 tokens" for each model class (base vs. instruction-tuned).
   - We include an estimated monthly quantity for budgeting. Invoices show actual quantity and net due.

Both approaches are compatible with a Blanket PO + monthly invoices. I'm attaching a short mapping workbook that shows how per-token tiers translate to line items and example invoice rows. Please take a look and tell us which path your AP prefers.

Attachments: Commit_Tier_Mapping.xlsx

If useful, Marissa can draft the specific wording to drop into your vendor form to make signature/acceptance straightforward.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Strategic Accounts (Americas)
Redwood Inference

From: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor supplier form & pricing format

Vivek — appreciate the options. A couple of clarifying points from our side:

- Our auditors are uncomfortable with open-ended overage lines unless there's a cap or an agreed escalation matrix. A per-unit overage rate is ok only if we can show a plausible upper bound to the CFO.
- Individual model classes on a PO create too many line items for our ERP (we try to limit to < 5 vendor lines per contract).
- The vendor form requires a checkbox confirming the vendor accepts "Net 60" terms and a PO reference field. If Redwood requires Net 30, we'll need the business case to justify faster payment.

Short ask: can Redwood propose a 3-line PO structure we can insert into the form (Base commitment, Overages capped at X% of commitment, Invoice cadence + payment terms)? If so, procurement can finish the vendor form and route to Finance.

Thanks — I can review a concrete line-item draft today.

John
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Systems

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>

John — thanks, and totally understand the ERP/audit constraints. Per our internal finance and legal review, here's a compact 3-line PO proposal that should map cleanly into your vendor form and satisfy auditors:

PROPOSED PO LINE ITEMS (example amounts for illustration; we’ll provide final numbers once commitment is confirmed):
1) Redwood Hosted API — Base Commitment (monthly) — $25,000
   - Description: Reserved capacity and committed usage credit for Redwood Hosted API (equivalent to ~500M text tokens).
2) Token Overages — Per 1,000,000 tokens — $45
   - Description: Applies to actual usage above monthly commitment. Monthly overages are invoiced with quantity and unit price.
3) Administrative / Integration Fee — One-time (or monthly as agreed) — $2,500
   - Description: Onboarding, SSO/KMS integration, and custom invoice mapping (if required)

We propose the following contractual clarifications to address your concerns:
- Overage cap: Overages in any single month will be capped at 150% of the Base Commitment invoice value unless parties agree in writing.
- Payment terms: Standard Redwood Net 60 for enterprise deals; if Acme requires Net 30 we can escalate to Finance for approval (typically for strategic commitments).
- Blanket PO: Redwood will accept a Blanket PO referencing the Master Purchase Agreement (MPA) and monthly invoices will reference the PO number and line items.

Attachments: PO-Lineitem-Proposal.pdf, SOW-draft.docx

Next steps: If that structure looks good, I can: (a) fill the vendor form fields with these exact line-item descriptions and values, (b) sign on Redwood's vendor form, and (c) issue the MPA/SOW for countersignature. Please confirm and I will push the vendorform back to you by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations
